Areca nut weevil / coffee bean weevil (Araecerus fasciculatus).

Description: a weevil roughly 3-5 mm long that attacks a wide range of dried stored products, including corn.

Damage: corn stored with the husk still attached is more susceptible to this pest than fully shelled, cleaned kernels. Larvae bore into the kernel and cob material; the pest is often found in storage areas with poor sanitation, particularly where grain dust residue has accumulated. Infestation levels in stored corn are generally described as moderate compared to major storage pests such as the lesser grain weevil, but it can still cause meaningful quality loss (CPC 2000).
